records.name: Wissahickon Interested Citizens Association
records.summary: Wissahickon Interested Citizens Association is one of the community organizations registered with the City to review nearby zoning and building proposals in the Lower Northwest part of the city. Neighbors can follow what is planned and speak up.
records.what_you_do: Members follow zoning and building proposals, send neighborhood concerns to the association, and join committees on parks, schools and beautification. The group also runs summer events such as movie nights and music in the park.

schedule.text: General membership meetings on the second Wednesday of each month, 7 to 8 pm, on Zoom. There is no meeting in August.

cost.text: Membership dues are $15 a year for one person or $25 for a household. Memberships run through the calendar year.

first_step.how: Register in advance on the meetings page for the next Zoom general membership meeting, the second Wednesday at 7 pm.
first_step.basis: Meetings are open to the public and the site says all are welcome, with a clear way in: register in advance to get the Zoom login.
first_step.what_to_expect: A meeting runs about an hour on Zoom, from 7 to 8 pm. Agendas list committee reports and other business, such as proposed bylaw updates. Joining costs $15 a year for one person or $25 for a household, and members can vote starting one month after they join.
first_visit_tips: Register on the meetings page ahead of time to get the Zoom login details.
Members must live inside the association's boundaries and be over 18, so check the boundaries on the membership page first.
Voting starts one month after you join, so join before a meeting if you want a say.

records.name: Wissahickon Neighbors Civic Association (WNCA)
records.summary: Wissahickon Neighbors Civic Association (WNCA) is a Registered Community Organization (RCO) in the Lower Northwest part of the city. The City asks developers to talk with RCOs about nearby zoning and building plans, so this is a way for neighbors to have a say.
records.what_you_do: Neighbors meet monthly, review zoning and building plans nearby, and help care for Wissahickon Neighbors Woodland through monthly cleanups. Members vote on neighborhood matters.

schedule.text: Neighborhood meetings on the third Thursday of each month, 7 to 8 pm, at Pilgrim Church. Woodland cleanups are monthly on the second Sunday, 10 am to noon.

cost.text: Yearly dues: $25 for one person, $40 for a household, $10 for seniors, students or low-income members, and $100 for a business.

first_step.how: Come to the next neighborhood meeting, the third Thursday at 7 pm at Pilgrim Church, 3815 Terrace St.
first_step.basis: Meetings are open to neighbors in person, and the site has a Join page and an updates sign-up, which together make a clear way in.
first_step.what_to_expect: Meetings run an hour at Pilgrim Church, and neighbors are welcome to attend. Woodland cleanups are held on Sunday mornings, a hands-on way to help the park while meeting neighbors. Membership dues are $25 a year for one person, and members are the ones who can vote on neighborhood matters.
first_visit_tips: Sign up for the newsletter on the site to hear about meetings and events.
Woodland cleanups are on the second Sunday of the month, so plan around that date.
Join online through the Join Today page if you want to vote.

records.what_you_do: Help with school based programs for students and families.

records.name: Eastwick Friends & Neighbors Coalition
records.summary: The Eastwick Friends & Neighbors Coalition is a group of neighbors who work on flooding, the Clearview Landfill cleanup, and the refinery land. It has posted public meetings and news since 2012, but its newest posts are from 2022, so check before you plan to come.
records.what_you_do: Send flooding reports, environmental concerns, and local news to the coalition, follow its updates by email, and join one of its action committees.

first_step.how: Sign up for updates with the Follow Blog via Email form on the coalition's blog home page.
first_step.basis: The site invites people to join email updates and an action committee, but it lists no current meetings or volunteer roles and gives no direct contact, so the way in is unclear.
first_step.what_to_expect: Past public meetings were posted as open to all and usually ran about two hours on weeknights, mostly in person at local venues. The newest posts are from 2022 and no upcoming meeting is listed, so ask before you plan to come.
first_visit_tips: Read the newest posts on the blog first, since the most recent items are from 2022.
Bring your flooding or environmental questions, since those are the coalition's main topics.

records.name: Eastwick United CDC
records.summary: Eastwick United CDC is a group of Eastwick residents working on local issues such as flooding, the Amazon warehouse on Elmwood Avenue, and the Hilco refinery cleanup. It is also a City-registered community organization. Its website lists no upcoming meetings, and its newest dated news is from April 2022.
records.what_you_do: Review local issues, such as proposed developments and flooding, and join the discussion on the group's issue pages.

first_step.how: Send a question through the contact form on eastwickunited.org to ask for the next community meeting date and Zoom link.
first_step.basis: The site lists no upcoming meetings, events or volunteer roles, and its only listed way in is a contact form, so the way to join is unclear.
first_step.what_to_expect: The last meeting listed on the site, in 2021, ran an hour on Zoom in the evening and let neighbors meet the board of directors. No current date is posted, so ask before you plan to attend.
first_visit_tips: Ask through the contact form for the next meeting date.
Read the issue pages on flooding, the Amazon warehouse and the airport expansion to see what the group is working on.

records.name: Empowered CDC
records.summary: Empowered CDC is one of the City's Neighborhood Advisory Committees in Southwest Philadelphia. Residents can get help finding City services and ways to get more involved in their neighborhood.
records.what_you_do: Help neighbors find City services and bring local needs to the City. The City's zoning review list also includes this organization under the Empowered Community Development Corporation name (see notes).

first_step.how: Call the office at 215-278-9782 and ask for help with a City service.
first_step.basis: The City flyer gives a phone number and office address for help, but the group's own website did not load, so meeting times and a clear way to join are unknown.
